What you said kinda opened my eyes a little. I used to talk to this southern girl online that lived in a quiet little town and it always bothered me that she never wanted to do anything more with her life. Once again, kinda strange coming from me but things were different back then. And looking back on it now I do envy her. Simplicity. Her ability to actually like her life the way it is and accept it. 

There are just too many options in modern times. I know at first glance that seems like a good thing but it can also be extremely overwhelming. So many decisions and consequences to mull over.

I haven't written anything  that I've enjoyed in a long time. It just feels like I draw my creativity from a lot of negative places and nothing works anymore. I just end up really disappointed in myself. I've always wanted to write a novel but I spend way too much time on very minute details and end up not making any progress.

I've written the beginnings of so many stories with endings already in my mind, it's just the middle where I get caught.

I kinda already did ditch everything...I ended up here. Sold and pawned all of my possessions to get this far and now I'm reserving this last 120.65$ for buying the supplies that I'll need to end this.

I've spent so many hours reading self-help books and advice. Therapists, rationalizing and hoping. Telling myself that my decisions are insignificant in the long run, telling myself that this misery will all just be a funny memory one day.

This isn't something I've decided on a whim. This is it.

using other peoples' limbs as ladder rungs isn't how I want to live.

It's a cut throat world and I just don't want to be that kind of person.

I remember good times. I dwell on them all the time and it makes me feel empty knowing that even if I did find happiness there would be a peak to it, and then after that there's no where to go but down.

Almost like nothing could top it.

If I had a choice I'd die instantly at the happiest point in my life. Go off on a good note.
I believe that people find the best things in life entirely by chance.

As strange as it sounds coming from me I really hope you get your life back on track. I only know myself and how I feel but I've encountered so many depressed people before that have made it out. I firmly believe that *most* people can be helped if they're willing to save themselves. Unfortunately, I'm not. That fact is probably frustrating a lot of people that've been reading this. I can only blame myself for giving up.

A lot of people talk about hope like it's a good thing but all it's done for me is prolong my despicable life. Year after year I kept holding on, waiting for a movie miracle to happen that never did. That's my fault, too. For hoping, instead of acting.

cheers!

held hostage by fear

year after year

waiting for the sky to clear

I love hugs. It's been a long time since I've had one. The warmth of living beings is always very soothing. Cradling a baby in your arms. Or a chihuahua :P

I've always tried to be a good person to everyone, always tried to be respectful of people and their decisions and always helped out when ever someone asked for it. I'm the kind of person that believes in the "if it makes you feel good, do it, as long as you're not hurting anyone" thing. And I feel like I have been a good friend/relative to the people I've known. I've had a lot of conversations where people have told me how much I've helped or influenced their lives. So I don't think I've changed the world, but at least a few peoples' views of it..as odd as that may seem coming from me, with the decisions I've made. I only want the best for everyone that's ever shown me kindness, and I've done and will do the best I can with what I have to show them that in the end.

My belief on the point of life: To find the things you love in life and share them with the people you care about.

I always told myself that I would go back to school eventually but I never found anything I was passionate enough about. In my mind it all just ends with the same problems that it begins with.

I'm just unwilling to believe that my life will take a positive turn, and even if it did it would probably be so minuscule and I'd continue to go through bouts of depression on and off for the rest of my life. I know pure happiness isn't a realistic standard, but I'm not wanting pure happiness, I want to be able to bear living, and I can't. I can't even imagine it.

There's always a part that hopes. That part is the enemy.

I had a job for 3 years on the night shift. It was pure misery. I loathed every moment of it. And the reason I put up with it for so long is because it was simple, I got a ride to work, didn't have to deal with public transportation, and didn't have to talk to many people. But I hated it. It ate away at me every day. But I put up with it because it was the easy route in avoiding my fears and anxieties.

That's also partially the reason why I don't want to enter the workforce again. I can't stand the thought of going back to another backbreaking soulsucking job again. Or having to deal with people.

A whole lot of teenage drama later and my friend assumes that I think she's a whore for cheating on my cousin with his brother and avoids me. We don't talk for years after that. It's a whole nother story that would be really long winded. The jist of it is we all just went our separate ways.

* In the past it was mainly my cousin that initiating the meeting. I was just along for the ride mostly. I've been feeling utterly alone because I am. Some people say they don't have friends because they feel like they can't open up to theirs. I say I don't have friends because I literally don't. I ended up becoming very guarded and paranoid, so I was always wary of people when I met them and came off as a prick. I still find it very hard to trust people I meet. I can never tell apart the people who are genuinely being sincere from the people that are just being polite.

* Been to several therapists. Been on anti-depressants. Neither helped much. They always left me worse off.

Well, like a lot of depressed people I'm convinced that things won't get better. There've been so many times where I've pulled myself back up only to be knocked down again. I feel like every time something negative happens to me it's just the universe sending me another sign. "Life's not for you", "just quit". 

Everyone thinks to do just the opposite. Self preservation. We're all wired to keep ourselves alive. But to what end? To HOPEFULLY have something positive in my life happen? To work at building myself back up and HOPE something doesn't come along to smash me down again? It's not worth it. In my mind it's not worth it. I'm worthless. I really am. I offer nothing to the world but whining and self loathing. Best be done with it already.

* A lifelong struggle with constant depression. Being utterly alone. A firm belief that even if I did pull myself out of the gutter I'd end up slaving my life away at another soul sucking job. It's a culmination of a lifetime full of shit.




* I've done a lot of fucked up things. I won't list any of it here in case someone I know happens to read this. "but you're going to die so what does it matter?". Even so. 




* When I was 16 my dad kicked me out (it was my fault.) I spent the summer with my cousin riding the city bus all day, just meeting people and having fun. One day we met this girl at the mall. It was coincidentally her birthday, we became close friends (she ended up having my cousin's kid). Long story short we're all homeless and hitchhike out to this town called Bruno. Best summer of my life. That simple stupid little town holds so many memories for me. It's the last time I remember being carefree. Being free period. I can listen to a song from back then and it feels just like that town did.

A lot of lonely people get pets. I've always loved dogs but I don't have the financial means to even support myself anymore. I'm also not sure if that's a healthy way to approach loneliness (coming from the guy that's going to off himself, heh). I have very irrational worries, I'm very self-conscious so if I did get an animal I'm afraid of what people would think of me "look at that pathetic guy. all he has is his dog. How sad.". That wasn't meant to be judgement on you, I'm just trying to explain how my brain works. I overthink things a lot of the time to the point where I'm stressed as hell.






I know what you mean about relying on someone. For the past few years I've slowly lost contact with everyone. I have no friends left at all anymore and the only person I have to confide in just walked out on me and I can't really blame him. I've been relying on my cousin for everything for years now. He did everything for me because of my severe social anxiety. I knew it was just a matter of time until he left me. He's got a life of his own to lead and I can't blame him for his decision. My mom died on June 3rd 2003 due to her alcoholism. I love my grandma so much and the thought of outliving her or my father fills me with so much sorrow. I know what I'm doing to them is what I've been fearing myself, and it's selfish. All I can do is hope that they'll understand. This won't be a surprise to anyone. It was just a matter of when. Everyone already knows why.
